chunks: Ali, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Ibn Azina, from Bukeyr who said:

I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) say: When a man divorces his wife, and two just witnesses witness it prior to her waiting period, so it is not for him that he should divorce her until she has completed her waiting period, except if he reverts to her.
ai.seo_question: What are the conditions for a valid revocable divorce and the husband's right to reconciliation in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi clarifies the procedural validity of revocable divorce (ṭalāq rajʿī) by requiring two just witnesses to attest to the husband's acceptance of the waiting period (ʿiddah). It establishes that the husband cannot issue a new divorce until the ʿiddah concludes, unless he first exercises his right of reconciliation (rajʿah), thereby preventing hasty or multiple divorces in quick succession. This ruling underscores the Shia emphasis on witness testimony as a condition for the legal finality of the divorce process during the interim period.

en.hubeali: Ali, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Ibn Azina, from Bukeyr who said,

‘I heard Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> sayig: ‘When the man divorces his wife, and two just witnesses witness it prior to her waiting period, so it is not for him that he should divorce her until she has completed her waiting period, except if he reverts to her’.
en.sarwar: 3. Ali has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from ibn ‘Udhaynah from Bukayr who has said the following: “

I once heard abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, saying, ‘If one divorces his wife in the presence of two just witnesses at a time when commencement of waiting period is possible, he then cannot divorce her before the end of waiting period unless he goes back to her.’”
